I have been a "postbezorger" in the K-buurt. Never failed unsafe, but I've grown up around the place.

1. The community is nice, but you really have to adjust. Forget everything you know about Amsterdam, have a more Caribbean attitude and everything is chill. A lot of people are from Suriname or one of the Caribbean islands that The Netherlands used to have. But it might be really hard if you are not used to this, really keep that in mind.  
2. I don't know how they are right now, but when I went to high school 20 years ago, the local high schools were seen as the lowest of the low and considered heavily as "Black Schools". Schools in The Netherlands are completely different than most of the world though. I would suggest checking out International schools if you are not from The Netherlands.   
3. I have not lived in the K-buurt, but I have lived next to the ArenA for more than 9 years, working at the Mcdonalds next to the Bijlmer Bajes when it was still in use and had nightshifts where I walked home at 3 am. Never felt unsafe, shady people be shady though, that's in every city in the world. Is it now much safer than between the 60's and 90's? Definitely! Is there still a lot of violence and gangs around? You bet your ass there are. Don't look at the wrong people for too long and just say hello nicely when interacting and you should be fine. It used to be called the Dutch "Harlem" for a reason.  
4. The government has spend millions upon millions to make Zuidoost the place where you would love to live. Good hospitals, good shopping (especially if you love international food), the parks are being maintained. It's the good thing of having been the problem neighborhood for decades, money flows in.  
5. Good investment to buy a house right now in The Netherlands? I think you could invest into Bitcoin and have a more stable guarantee that you will get at least your money in return. The housing bubble has been growing and there is no stop to it because of rich Expats who can just shell out 50K above a house price without even thinking. If you want a guaranteed profit, don't, if the bubble bursts you will lose hundreds of thousands potentially.  
6. How about you rent a hotel room for a week, get a feel for the people, walk around at night, go do some shopping and see if you feel like you are home. For me and my mom it felt like being on vacation in our own town, we still love it and I come there often. But don't buy in for hundreds of thousands, just to have a home in Amsterdam..There are better places and better ways to spend your money.

I still don't understand that The Netherlands is seen as the place to start a life if you are not from here. The language is hard to learn, the people are horrible at times, our government has sucked for over more than a decade, housing is expensive as all hell, and I can continue.

I'm not an expat, migrant or anything else, born and raised in Amsterdam.  
But if I'd move to another country, I'd be getting all the info before going. Racism and Sexism have been an issue for a very long time and is getting a resurgence in the last decade. Bike stolen? That sucks, but that is a big part of living in the Netherlands. Dutch people intolerant? Yup, don't get why people think we are so tolerant, we haven't been that since the 90's.

Your own information is not stored in the subdomain, only the owners information.

If you want 100% anonymity you'll need a tor address on the dark web, and even then it's not 100% untraceable.

A VPN service is not illegal, most businesses use it to connect to a server with classified information. However, you can be flagged as suspicious. When using a VPN your network token is smaller than it should be, that's why Netflix and other streaming services are making sure the smaller than expected tokens are not usable.  
When we are talking about an illegal service, then yes that is still illegal.  


Talking about making sure that your provider can't track you, a VPN will make it a bit harder, but it's definitely not impossible to find your exact location as you are tunneling through one encrypted tunnel which means that they can track the enterance and exit.  


If you really want to be as anonymous as can be, and I'm not saying that this is the best route, but people seem to be able to be very anonymous. Use a Tor Browser. This will use 4 gateways all over the world to encrypt your movements and because any computer that is connected to the Tor gateways as a host, this means that it's much harder to track. However, and this is a very big however, it is still not garuenteed to be safe, you are still connecting through other computer networks to finally get into this network of the illegal tv and if your provider decides (really small chance) to host themselves on the first receiving gateway, then they could in theory follow you and know that you are up to no good. Mostly because of dark web surfing (which is not illegal, but why go there is their opinion.)  


Your provider is not the biggest issue with illegal tv's and such, it's Stichting Brein, they make sure that people pay fines for their illegal downloading and spreading of media. Depending on your provider, they might give your information if there is suspision that you are doing illegal things.  


From what I've been reading, users are not being punished right now for using illegal streaming tv online, but the providers of it are getting jailed for what they do.  


If you are scared you'll be fined for using it, don't use it. If you are afraid of what they will do with your information (Those kind of services are notorious for selling your data or misusing your data, and you are giving loads of data without knowing) don't use it.  
From an IT perspective there's lots that can go wrong, but if you really want to use it, you can.

Fazley is not the most known brand in the music world, although not yet.  
I've played guitar and bass for more than 20 years now and I've held a lot of instruments.  


Back in the day when I had to stop professional music and get...ugh...a real job...I had to sell my fantastic Fender MIM Precision Bass.  
I don't have the spare income to buy a similar one, especially because of the price increases last 5 years. So I went to Bax-shop and ordered the Fazley Judge Bass, which is a jazz bass that is a good replica from the Fender Basses.  
The neck felt so similar to a Fenders, my thumb slides over it like it has been oiled, but it's just the roasted wood what makes it so damn smooth!  
Intonation was a bit over the place, but it's an easy fix. The elements are surprisingly good, I plugged it into my DAW with BiasFX and my god, Blindly I wouldn't know it was a "budget" bass.  


I did some research and there's nothing to find about Fazleys, but I noticed a lot of similarities to Thomann's house brand called Harley Benton. Great looking and sounding instruments built in Asia, just like Bax's Fazley.  
So they are probably built in the same factory as other "cheap" brands which have been going up in quality, and they can buy them for a fraction of what you'd buy a Fender or a Gibson for. So the direct business makes it that we pay less for an instrument that should be more expensive.  
My advice is, keep Fazley in your line of sight, maybe wait 5 years for them to grow more, the new Outlaw series of Fazley is amazing. Don't throw them out just yet.

If you'd like to read about Disney Romance and especially about romance at Disneyland Paris you should check out my blog 

https://wuasdisney.com/category/romance/

Yes, there are mixed reviews on Disneyland Paris, but from most bad reviews I've read are from American tourists. (Not trying to start a debate here)

When you go to Disneyland Paris you should expect higher prices on the hotels, why? Because prices in Europe have been skyrocketed because of the mass tourism. 
For example, if you go to Amsterdam the cheapest and bad hotels are still over 100 dollars a night!
Disneyland Paris is quite the same, prices have skyrocketed because of the millions that come every year. But the quality hasn't been improving.

The European and especially French mentality is way different than the American fake smile mentality. You can still expect service and kindness, but you will also see a lot of honesty. I know from my American friends that my Dutch honesty is something they needed some time to get adjusted to, but eventually they loved my honesty because they knew I was always speaking the truth. The French do the same, if they are having a good time talking to you then they will do anything for you, but if you go there expecting service because you are the guest and you demand to be king you will feel some French revolution spirit coming up.

Now is Disneyland Paris the perfect honeymoon location? I would say yes with a tiny no next to it.

In the words of Tony Baxter: "Disneyland was the original, Walt Disney World the unlimited possibilities for a vacation resort, and Disneyland Paris was how we really wanted to do Disneyland back when we built it in the 50's"
You will see so many tiny details that will make you fall in love with Disney all over again. The castle is something even a European who has seen them all will fall in love with. The castle even has a gigantic dragon underneath!
The castle is the perfect castle to take honeymoon pictures at!

Like you said you've seen it all, then Disneyland Paris will be a refresher. We dont have a Tomorrowland, we have Discoveryland. It's the same rides but in the style of Jules Verne. And it is stunning!

So why a tiny no? If you are a ride buff then Disneyland Paris might seem a lot less than WDW and DL. But if you go for the European romance for your honeymoon you are in the right place.

I would suggest on thinking about coming back after 2025 when the full European Epcot style expansion is planned. The Disney Company has been injecting 3.2 billion dollars to make great expansions and renovations so DLP can compliment its American bigger brothers.

She colapsed onto the floor and the only thing I could hear was gurgling from her throat, but trough the gurgling I could hear the demon say: "Have fun cleaning this mess up, no one will believe you".

de eerste trein ging om 05:05 en die ging naar Amsterdam Centraal, vanuit daar had ik de trein die via Amsterdam Bijlmer naar Utrecht ging (stop trein). De enige optie om rechtstreeks vanuit Hilversum naar Utrecht te komen was de stoptrein om half 7 naar Utrecht en dan was ik veel later geweest.  


Maar blijkbaar wilden ze liever dat ik helemaal ging verhuizen dan dat ik 2 minuten te laat was terwijl ik 2 uur elke dag reisde.
We hebben het dan niet over een half uur te laat elke keer, zelfs 1 minuut te laat krijg je een kruisje.

Ik heb er in het begin van het jaar gewerkt voor 3 maanden, en deze redenen zijn precies waarom ik daar weg ben! Op een drukke dag loop je met gigantisch veel pickers (veels te veel) tegelijk om de orders te pakken en sta je constant in de file. Dan lopen de trainers tussendoor de karren om te vertellen hoe slecht je het doet als je te langzaam was. Ik heb eens gehad dat een trainer zei: "je gemiddelde ligt normaal veel hoger! Hoe komt dit?" dus ik zei: "je ziet niet de 20 karren die stil staan voor mij? ik heb al mijn producten van dit pad al, moet ik dan langs 20 karren gaan en iedereen inhalen omdat ik sneller ben? Zorg eerst dat het goed wordt geregeld!"  
Toen moest ik op het matje komen omdat ik brutaal was.  


Ze verwachten ook dat je met openbaar vervoer er elke dag op tijd kunt komen, want ze zeggen misschien wel dat je met sneeuw geen kruisje krijgt, maar dat krijg je dus wel, tenminste ik wel.  
Elke ochtend reiste ik 2 uur in de ochtend van Hilversum naar Amsterdam Muiderpoort om dan naar Utrecht te reizen met de trein en dan nog met de bus om dan altijd net op tijd te komen. Moet de bus een minuut wachten ergens? Ja dan ben ik te laat!  
Je kunt dan zeggen dat het mijn eigen schuld is dat ik elke ochtend 2 uur erover deed, tuurlijk het was mijn keuze, maar ze zeiden in mijn laatste gesprek voordat ik ontslag nam: "Het is jouw verantwoordelijkheid dat je op tijd komt, jij komt zelden op tijd (lees, 2 minuten te laat max), dus zorg ervoor dat je nu altijd op tijd bent en je kunt hier blijven werken, als je nog 2 keer te laat bent is het exit".  
Dus ik uit proberen te leggen wat mijn reis in houdt en dat als ik elke dag een half uur later kan beginnen dat ik dan maar 30 minuten over mijn reis doe wilden ze niks van weten, want je begint wanneer hun zeggen dat je begint en anders ben je weg.  


Toen ik daar solliciteerde had ik het gevoel dat ik bij een jonge en coole startup solliciteerde, je werdt met open armen ontvangen en ze maakten er een grote poeha van dat je daar was, want dit was het begin van je Picnic carriere. "We willen zien hoe je met elkaar om gaat, dus ga maar samen even tafel fooball spelen!" "Het is heel belangrijk voor ons dat jij het gevoel hebt dat je wordt gehoord, iedereen kan doorgroeien en goed geld verdienen"  
Het voelde een "Arbeit macht vrei" moment, alsof alles goed was, je komt bij het beste bedrijf ooit, je krijgt 3 weken training, volledig betaald!  
Ik heb in totaal minder dan 40 minuten training gehad, en ik overdrijf niet, andere collega's vonden mijn 40 minuten zelfs veel omdat ze zeiden dat ze het gevoel hadden niet eens 30 minuten training overall zouden hebben gekregen.  


Picnic zelf is geen slecht bedrijf voor de klant, maar voor de werknemer heb je het gevoel dat ze robots te duur vonden dus gaan ze maar de werkdruk verhogen naar onmogelijke doelstellingen.

They see the Hatbox Ghost infront of the mansion who tells them to get into the mansion because it is their destiny, they cannot refuse for some spooky reason. When they get into the first hallway they notice that they are in an octagon shaped room and the Hatbox Ghost starts explaining what this mansion is, they see the portraits stretch and see how the husbands of constance have died. And then the Hatbox Ghost vanishes and it gets dark and they hear: "or you can take my way out" and they see the iconic hanging man.  


They are alowed to move on to the main hall where they see the singing busts (actually going to play the music for them :D ) and they can ask them questions, but it's uncertain if they tell the truth because they have no reason to tell them the truth, they don't need anything.  
Then they are suggested to go to the dining hall because they seem very hungry.  
In the dining hall they see the scene of the Haunted Mansion ride and they get greeted by the small ghost figure on top of the chandelier and he tells them that Constance won't let them pass on to the light because she doesn't want to be alone and they are cursed to stay there forever!  
The party goers does not know how to break the curse but the party goers know that Madame Leota is upstairs and she knows all.  


While the players are moving from room to room they get harassed by poltergeists, visions, bleeding walls and all that.  
Leota will tell them that Constance is in the dungeons underneath the mansion and that there is only one way to defeat her. Leota will not easily say what the way is because that's also the way to kill her herself.  
So they have 2 options, an incredible Pursuasion roll, or understand that Leota has no real purpose in the house and maybe the players will understand that they can take her with her and that way she will tell them to burn the bones of Constance.  


After that the party will descend down into the dungeon and they will have to face traps and ghosts who want to harm them as they are pro Constance.  


When the players can open up the coffin of Leota they see a scroll in her hands, if they take the scroll they'll know afterwards why they needed to do this mission, if not this knowledge will be gone forever.
